xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3552: Simplify the review pipeline to the operator's flow — drop speculative layers, keep the two real protections

plan.title: Simplify the review pipeline to the operator's flow — drop speculative layers, keep the two real protections
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5

metadata.upstreamDependencyNote: PAN-3512 (strike-pan-3512) is actively implementing the recordReviewVerdict write door, its dispatch-not-drop semantics, and the fallback kill-conditional while this plan is authored. Items tagged metadata.upstreamDependency PAN-3512 must run pan sync-main PAN-3552 first and build on the merged write-door contract rather than reimplementing any part of it.
metadata.sizeJustification: The five drops are entangled in the same modules — review-agent.ts, review-convoy.ts, review-status.ts, pan-dir/record.ts, parked/resolver.ts and deacon.ts each carry two or more of them — so independently shippable sibling issues would rebase-conflict on nearly every item. The plan keeps one workspace and encodes the real file-sharing dependencies as blocks edges, which serializes exactly the items that touch the same files and leaves the rest free.

narratives.Problem: The review pipeline accreted eight layers over six months. An operator-commissioned evidence review found that no forged verdict has ever occurred — the threat model is trusted agents on a single-operator machine — while every real incident is verdict loss or row drift. The speculative layers cost real reliability: on 2026-08-05 a duplicate review dispatch flipped the row to reviewing at review-agent.ts:546, the parent correctly refused to re-signal an already-finalized run, nothing reset the row, and the only exit was a manual pan review request.
narratives.Proposal: Cut the pipeline to the operator's stated flow — convoy reviewers do their job, they tell the synthesis parent, the parent tells the work agent to ship it or hands over the feedback — plus the two protections that answer observed incidents: the synthesis artifact as verdict of record, and recordReviewVerdict as the single write door with head-anchor staleness rejection. Drop the discovery fork and cache-miss detector, selective re-review and per-reviewer verdicts, the branch-invalidation sweep, and the stall sweeper's residual actor event surface. Add the reconciliation today's drift evidence proves is missing: dispatch consults the verdict of record before mutating the row, the deacon reconciler covers reviewing rows through the write door, and a same-head converge stops re-gating an already-recorded test verdict.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do NOT remove src/lib/conversations/session-fork.ts — conversation summary forks depend on it; only the review caller goes.
- Do NOT remove or weaken recordReviewVerdict, its head-anchor staleness rejection, or the verdict-of-record contract.
- Do NOT remove synthesizeReviewFromReports, the minimal dead-parent fallback that reads the four reports and writes synthesis.md.
- Do NOT remove checkStalledReviewParents, the observability-only parent liveness watch.
- Do NOT remove deliverReviewVerdictFeedback or any part of feedback delivery — PR comment, feedback file, and pan tell all stay.
- Do NOT remove resolveParkedPopulation or the God View's parked read; only the actor-shaped event surface goes.
- Do NOT add HMAC signing, sandboxing, attestation sidecars, or any cryptographic verdict provenance — forgery is a non-threat in this deployment.
- Do NOT drop SQLite columns or write a schema migration; the removed agent-state columns stay inert.
- Do NOT give the stall sweeper any ability to spawn, stop, kill, message, dispatch, clear, or reset.
- Do NOT change the convoy contract in roles/review.md beyond removing references to dropped machinery.
- Do NOT reimplement PAN-3512's write-door work — its dispatch-not-drop semantics and fallback kill-conditional are upstream of this plan; sync main and build on them.
- Do NOT backfill or migrate durable records that still carry reviewerVerdicts or conflictsSince; readers tolerate the extra keys.

autoDecisions.summary: Planned as one xBRIEF with plan.metadata.sizeJustification rather than sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: The swarm contract prefers sibling issues, but review-agent.ts, review-convoy.ts, review-status.ts, pan-dir/record.ts, parked/resolver.ts and deacon.ts are each touched by two or more of the five drops, so parallel siblings would conflict on nearly every item. Blocks edges serialize exactly the shared-file items instead.

autoDecisions.summary: No attestation-removal item: HMAC attestation and the sandbox boundary are already absent from main at 299d98db34.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-3511 merged on 2026-08-05 without them; the only surviving mention is roles/review-security.md telling reviewers not to request them. The architecture doc item asserts the absence instead of deleting code that does not exist.

autoDecisions.summary: handleReviewDiscoveryReady is renamed rather than deleted.
autoDecisions.rationale: It carries the PAN-3368 per-lane recovery that the same-run parent resume depends on; deleting it outright would strand review-agent.ts:716. The fork parameters go, the recovery stays.

autoDecisions.summary: The stall sweeper's detection and recommendation surface is kept; only sweep.action and sweep.unparked go.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue body — the operator's decided scope, later than the evidence report's harder 4.2 recommendation — says to finish removing the actor surface and keep the parked-population read for the God View.

autoDecisions.summary: SQLite agents columns are left in place as inert columns instead of being migrated away.
autoDecisions.rationale: The agents table is a rebuildable cache per docs/AGENT-STATE-PLANES.md, so a destructive column drop buys nothing and risks a boot failure on an existing database.

autoDecisions.summary: The four items touching the verdict write door are sequenced behind PAN-3512 and marked with metadata.upstreamDependency.
autoDecisions.rationale: strike-pan-3512 is implementing the write door, dispatch-not-drop, and the fallback kill-conditional in the same files in parallel. Planning on top of its contract — with a mandatory pan sync-main before those items — avoids duplicating its scope and avoids a rebase fight over review-verdict-writer.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: Convergence reuses SYNTHESIS_ARTIFACT_FRESH_MS rather than defining a new freshness window.
autoDecisions.rationale: That constant already encodes belongs-to-the-current-review-cycle; a second window would be a new drift surface in a simplification issue.
